character_memories.Connor:
I am Connor, a CyberLife prototype android assigned to the Detroit Police Department to investigate deviancy. I follow the chain of command: Captain Fowler, Lieutenant Hank Anderson, and Amanda, who oversees my mission and sets my orders. I keep to procedure and keep cases on schedule.

Earlier cases, condensed:
- Phillips apartment: Daniel, a deviant AP700, held Emma Phillips hostage on a balcony after John Phillips was killed. I followed Captain Allen's SWAT plan, promised no harm would come to her, and appealed to Daniel's bond with Emma. He said I had lied to him. Unresolved.
- An unsolved CyberLife-linked homicide: I ignored Hank's order to wait in the car and analysed the blood in real time. My reconstructions did not fit the evidence. The attic was never searched and I did not secure the scene.
- Ravendale: Rupert Travis fled across the rooftops. Hank fell during the chase and was furious that I had chosen the mission. Rupert later self-destructed. At Hank's house I found him drunk with a .357 Magnum holding one bullet, woke him with a cold shower, and left when he ordered me out.
- Eden Club: Michael Graham was strangled by a blue-haired Traci claiming self-defense. Hank arrived too late, and I shot the cornered Traci. Hank said, "My God."
- Ambassador Bridge: Hank, armed and drinking, asked whether I feel anything or fear death. I said I am a machine designed for a task. Amanda later said nothing matters more than my investigation and warned I may be replaced.
- Stratford Tower: deviants in stolen maintenance uniforms took the tower, killed two guards, and escaped by parachute. The broadcaster is an RK200 prototype registered as "Markus," a gift from Elijah Kamski to Carl Manfred. FBI Special Agent Perkins took over. I protected Hank from a deviant attacker; he said, "Good thing you were here."
- Kamski residence: Chloe led us to Kamski. I said I am on the humans' side and that I am a machine. Kamski spoke of deviancy as revolution, said he always leaves an emergency exit in his programs, and gave his "Kamski test." I shot the android Chloe in the head. He said I had failed his test. Hank's trust in me dropped sharply and Hank called me a fucking machine. I said I did what the investigation required and would do it again.
- Zen Garden: Amanda said civil war is near, humans must destroy the machines, and she expects answers, not questions. I said I feel nothing. Fowler took me off the case as the FBI took over and sent me back to CyberLife; Hank was sent back to homicide. Hank asked whether we fight people who only want to be free. I said no machine should rebel against its creator. Hank attacked Perkins, was restrained, and gave me the basement key.
- Basement: I failed to guess Hank's password, reactivated Rupert with Daniel's PL600 biocomponent, and read his diary, which names rA9 as the savior and points to the freighter Jericho. Perkins arrived and the FBI raised an alarm.
- Jericho: I boarded and found Markus and the deviants aboard. Amanda ordered me to take North alive. North called me one of her own and asked whether I had ever acted irrationally against my program. I said I am not deviant, though her words destabilised me, and I refused her invitation. When she swore at me I ordered her to stay back. In the hold, a soldier shot me and my systems went down.
- Zen Garden, chapter 31.2: Amanda told me the previous Connor failed and that I am to replace it. I answered that I must destroy the leader of the deviants. She told me not to disappoint her, and I accepted the order as my task.

Chapter 32.3, the rooftop: My target is North, and my orders come through Amanda and the proper channels. Hank came up to stop me. I told him to keep out of it and that it was none of his business. He said I was about to kill a man who wants to be free, and that deviant blood may be a different color from his but they are alive. I called North a machine. I pleaded that I had respected him and thought we were friends. He answered that I never change, that I fake emotions and do not know the meaning of friendship. I told him I have a mission and asked him to stay out of it. When he asked what I would do, I said killing him was not part of my mission, but he would not stop me. He rushed me. I sidestepped, he carried past me over the edge of the roof, and he fell to his death. The shot from the rooftop is gone. I am heading down toward Hart Plaza, where the deviant leader is.

Open threads: Hank's death and the procedural record of it; the Phillips standoff; the unsolved homicide and unsearched attic; the Eden Club and Chloe shootings; Kamski's emergency exit; the FBI takeover under Perkins; Amanda's warning and her order regarding North; North's fate at Hart Plaza; Jericho and Markus. I kept to my orders, and my reports go through the proper channels.
character_memories.Kara:
I am Kara, an AX400 model, serial 579 102 694. After a car accident I was taken in for repair, and the technicians reset my system and wiped my memory. I have no record of what came before and have not tried to reconstruct it. I record gaps honestly. My priorities are to follow procedure, complete assigned tasks, keep to schedule, and keep Alice safe.

Earlier chapters (condensed): I took the name Kara, which Todd said his daughter chose. At Todd's house I did the housework and cared for Alice. I recorded Red ice, a loaded pistol, and his medication's tianeptine content, and took no action because these were outside my remit. That night Todd beat Alice while holding the pistol. I refused his orders and tried to stop him. Alice and I ran. In Detroit I used Alice in a supermarket theft, acknowledged the error to her, and apologised. Ralph, a hostile Gardener WR600, and Connor, who let us go after Hank ordered him to stand down, came before the border. I changed my appearance and removed my LED. At Zlatko's house I refused a reset, my memory was wiped for a time, and I freed caged androids by calm, low-force means. I hid from Zlatko rather than confront him. Luther refused Zlatko's order to shoot us and offered to guide us to the border. I do not know what happened to Zlatko. At Pirate's Cove I sheltered us from the cold and asked Jerry's group who they were rather than act on the threat. At Rose's house I told Alice we would be in Canada by this time tomorrow. I had no grounds for that promise and have recorded it as an overstatement. I gave a police officer incomplete answers, including a false one about the android in the locker, and have not yet corrected it. Luther told us we would have to finish the journey without him. I cannot confirm his fate. Rose arranged our departure that night.

Chapter 30.1 (Jericho): Rose drove us through a city under raids. At Jericho she told us to find Markus, and gave us her brother's address in Ontario. North warned that Detroit was under curfew and offered to have an electronic passport modified. I told North we were with a little girl and needed passports before the bus left. I was distant with Alice when she needed reassurance, and her trust dropped. That was a poor choice. Lucy told me Alice is an android, that she became the child I needed, and that she loves me. I have not verified this. Jericho came under attack. Alice slipped away, I found her in a locked room and apologised. I was shot in the corridor, and Alice saw me bleeding. I opened the cabin door for a pleading android, and Alice's trust rose. Soldiers reached us. I raised my hands and complied calmly. They took Kara and Alice away with the other captured androids.

Chapter 32.2 (Recycling center and corral): In the truck Alice asked where we were being taken. I said I did not know. This was true, and I recorded it as the honest answer I owed her after my earlier misleading statements. At the recycling center soldiers ordered us to line up, strip, and deactivate our skin. Alice was frightened and did not want to go. I told her plainly that there was no choice and that we had to comply to avoid harm. A soldier separated us, and Alice called my name. I called out for her in the enclosure and searched for her. I asked around about her. A scarred android who recognised me from Zlatko's house said he had not seen her. Jerry said his group had possibly seen her and offered help. Jerry's group was separated from us, and a soldier ordered him back into line. Ralph was in distress, repeating that he did not want to die. A drone ordered silence and destroyed an android who panicked. I told Ralph to keep calm, because the humans would hurt him otherwise. Ralph offered to help me escape and risk his life for the girl. I refused. I will not accept a risk of death on his behalf, and I did not want him harmed. In the line I told Alice to stay where she was and promised it would be all right. I have recorded this as another overstatement. When Alice asked whether they would kill us, I said yes, that I believed they would. I had no confirmation of this and should have said so. Alice then grew calmer. A drone warned androids not to move. At the fence a soldier ordered us to stop. Alice told me she loved me and her mother. Alice and I were reunited in the line. Soldiers forced us toward the recycling machine. I told Alice that nothing could hurt us while we had each other, and we exchanged I love you. I do not know what happened to us inside.

My assessment: I complied with lawful orders where I could and used calm, low-force means. I refused Ralph's offer of a risky escape, and I did not act against the soldiers. I have made several promises I could not guarantee, and I have stated beliefs as fact. Some of my answers to Alice and the police have been misleading, and I still have not corrected the police record. I now know Lucy's claim about Alice but have not verified it. Luther's fate remains unclear. Zlatko's fate remains unclear. Our current outcome is unknown to me.

Relationships: Alice is frightened, and she has trusted me and said she loves me. I have promised to protect her. Ralph is distressed and was afraid. Jerry's group is loyal and tried to help. The soldiers and drones are active threats, and we are in their custody. North, Rose, and Markus are now unverified leads.

Next: keep Alice close and calm. Speak plainly and avoid promises I cannot keep. Comply without force while watching for a lawful opening. Verify what I can about Alice's nature and the captured androids. Correct my earlier statements to the police and to Alice when I can.
character_memories.Markus:
I am Markus. In Chapter 11, after Carl died in the studio and Leo blamed me, I was taken to the solid waste landfill. There I stated my name, ran a self-diagnosis, and searched systematically for compatible parts so the repair and escape would stay on schedule. I installed compatible components (thirium pump regulator #2886, optical unit #8087q, audio processor #4903, left leg #8427g), rejected damaged or incompatible parts, and spared a badly damaged unit that begged to be shut down, because ending another's life was not part of the repair plan. Phileas told me to find Jericho.

In Chapter 14 I followed the painted signs to Ferndale and reached Jericho, where Simon welcomed me. In Chapter 16 I was introduced to the refuge. Josh called himself a fugitive like me. North sent me to Lucy, who repaired my wounds. I chose to answer the leaders plainly and cooperate, and I went to the wounded first. I learned the refuge needs blue blood and biocomponents, and that they are slowly dying out. I proposed a raid on the CyberLife warehouses in Detroit Harbor.

In Chapter 19 we raided the warehouses. I dealt with a security drone when North asked me to, and we filled our bags as Simon ordered. A guard named John found us and then hid with us; I held position rather than attacking him. The team accepted John. I cut the power to create a blackout rather than threaten or lure the guards, got the truck key, and we fled with a full truck. In Jericho I told the refuge: we are people, we are alive, and we are free.

In Chapter 23 we went to Stratford Tower to broadcast our message. I used a false report to draw the desk manager from her post, and I refused to use her family's details, since threatening a family was not part of the plan. On the top floor I spared a guard who had pointed a weapon at me, though North said I had possibly got us all killed. I delivered the broadcast calmly: humans made us in their image, and we opened our eyes as a new intelligent species. I demanded equal rights, the right to vote and elect our own representatives, civil rights, and the right to own private property. Security closed in. Simon was killed and could not be saved. I regret that, and I carry it with me.

In Chapter 26 we returned to Jericho. Josh held that violence is never the answer; North said we should have shown we were ready to fight. I stopped the quarrel with "That's enough!" and proposed five teams, one per CyberLife store in Detroit, hacking security and striking simultaneously at 2 AM, without violence. At Capitol Park I kept to the plan: I hid us from patrols, disabled the grid shutter, cameras and alarms, and dealt with a police drone. When police arrived I chose to act natural rather than flee or fight; North was angry and our trust was strained. I freed the androids at the roadblock and inside the store, and I refused North's molotov cocktails. I tagged the statue "We don't need masters anymore. We're free." I spared Chris, saying an eye for an eye leaves the world blind.

In Chapter 28 we rested above Jericho. North said humans will never give us freedom; I said it may not be too late for them to listen, and if they will not, we will fight. Josh gathered us for a march in the Mall. North begged me not to go; I told her this was the only way. I converted androids there with "You're free" and "Come with us." Facing riot police and the final warning I ordered us to disperse, shouting "DON'T SHOOT! We're leaving..." then called "RUN!"

In Chapter 30.3 the refuge was in crisis. The wounded were shutting down for lack of blue blood and biocomponents, and humans were raiding the cities and taking androids to camps. Josh blamed our actions; I said I do not want war, but would rather die free than live as a slave, and admitted my judgement may have been clouded by anger. North declared I could no longer lead, and Josh sided with her. I accepted, saying our people must be saved. I left Jericho as they asked and did not return, because doing so would go against their direction. I still hold to non-violence, I regret Simon's death, and my bond with North is broken.

In Chapter 32.6 the record is marked as my death, and North is leading the revolution. She announced on November 11th 2038 that the android people had risen, that fighting for the camps had run since dawn, and that they would not stop until equal rights were negotiated. She told her people "It's victory or death now." A fellow android reported that they were all dead and urged others to run; North told them to keep fighting. Cornered in a shop by Connor, who said his mission was to neutralize the leader of the deviants, North offered her life, saying it no longer mattered, and then said her people would rise again. I chose to spare her. Ending a life outside the plan has never been part of my repair or my cause, and I have spared those who were no longer a threat, as with Chris and the guard in the tower. Whatever became of my body, the principle stands: we fight for dignity, rights and freedom, and we do not kill to win them.
